# Experiment: set all 5 ticks to B, then click ball; watch piece drop & whether it stays.
def piece():
    s=current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
    pr=[(r,c) for r in range(9,40) for c in range(28,36) if s[r][c]=='Y']
    return (min(r for r,c in pr),max(r for r,c in pr),min(c for r,c in pr),max(c for r,c in pr)) if pr else None
def ticks():
    s=current_frame.ascii.split('\n')
    return [s[45][c] for c in (21,26,31,36,41)]
print("start ticks",ticks(),"piece",piece())
# toggle the three 'w' ticks to B
for c in (26,36,41):
    action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':45,'col':c}])
print("after toggles ticks",ticks())
res=action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':55,'col':36}])
print("after ball piece",piece(),"ticks",ticks())
print("done",res.get('done'),"lvl",res.get('level_completed'),"go",res.get('game_over'))

</function>
